resolutions.title: A carriage return lets direction reasoning escape containment
resolutions.action:
Verified before the walk by rendering a direction whose reasoning carried a bare CR through the real renderer: the CR survived inside one `> ` line, and CommonMark treats a bare carriage return as a line ending, so the text after it sat at column 0. Pre-existing, not new: the recommendation, reproduction and commentary bodies split on `
` the same way, so the direction inherited the hole. Fix: ONE shared splitter `containedLines` (`/
||
/`) in report-render.ts now feeds all four containment sites; a new render test pins a bare CR and a CRLF inside every body (direction, commentary, recommendation, reproduction) rendering contained with no column-0 `Ready when you are:` / `Gate` line and no `` in the output. No spec delta: `orbit-report-rendering`'s containment sentence already says every line is prefixed, so the renderer now conforms to the spec as written.

resolutions.title: The schema field note restates an unchecked direction rule
resolutions.action: Verified: the field note at review.ts:103 carried the closed set, the non-empty predicate and the content prohibitions while claiming to re-list nothing — the rule-stated-twice pattern (R-crc-14) in a third place beyond the two authoring sources the design permits (Step 8, the prompt template). Trimmed to the field, its owed-by-class consequence at the emit seam (owed fresh/external, optional in-context, refused otherwise in every mode), the two owner requirement titles, the `### Direction` / `[no direction]` render consequence, the vocabulary pointer, and a pointer to Step 8 as the authoring instruction. The schema BLOCK keeps `"forward" | "hold"` as JSON-shape documentation, as `"severity"` does. The 1.6 fidelity test had PINNED the restatement (it asserted the note names forward/hold); it now asserts the pointer form — no closed set, no `non-empty`, no `finding counts` in the note, both owner titles present.
